title: Even the spoils of war carried a share for others.
subtitle: Even a win carries other people's share
then: The surah returns to the question it opened with: the spoils. One fifth was set aside, with shares named for the Prophet's ﷺ relatives, orphans, the needy and the stranded traveler. The Prophet ﷺ said: {trap}hand over even the needle and the thread,{/trap} and told one man that {idea}even an arrow pulled from your own side gives you no more right to it than your brother.{/idea}
now: The bonus lands. The business has its best quarter. The house sells above asking. {idea}Before it all gets spent, remember the orphan, the neighbor who is short, the traveler stuck far from home.{/idea} Their share was written into the win.
old: I worked for this. It's all mine.
new: What I gain is not only mine. Others have a share in what Allah gives me.
try: From your next income, set aside a small portion first for someone in need, before anything else.

title: If you had planned the meeting, you would have missed it.
subtitle: Badr happened without anyone's appointment
then: Ibn Az-Zubayr explained that {trap}if they had set a date and learned the enemy's numbers, they would not have come.{/trap} Allah brought them together without plan, so that {idea}those who chose disbelief chose it after clear proof, and those who believed did so on clear proof.{/idea} Ibn Kathir adds: faith is the life of the heart.
now: The best things in your life may not have been on your calendar: the stranger who became your spouse, the layoff that led to the right job. {idea}If you had seen them coming, you might have run.{/idea} Look back and notice His arranging.
old: The important things in my life happened because I planned them.
new: Many turning points came without my planning. Allah arranged them.
try: Write down one unplanned event that changed your life for the better. Thank Allah for it.

title: He showed them few in a dream, to keep your courage.
subtitle: Allah knows what a heart can carry
then: Mujahid said Allah showed the Prophet ﷺ the enemy as few in a dream. {reward}He told his Companions and their resolve grew.{/reward} Had they seen the true size, the verse says, {trap}they would have lost heart and fallen into dispute.{/trap} Allah knows what is in the chests.
now: You did not know how hard the degree, the new baby, the caregiving years would be. If you had known everything at the start, you might never have begun. {idea}Not knowing it all was a mercy.{/idea}
old: I wish I had known how hard this would be.
new: Allah showed me only what I could carry. Not knowing was a mercy.
try: Think of something hard you're in now. Focus only on today's piece of it, and ask Allah for strength for that.

title: Each side looked few to the other.
subtitle: Perception, shaped for a decree
then: Ibn Mas'ud said the enemy looked so few that {idea}he asked the man next to him, do you think they are seventy?{/idea} The man said a hundred. A captive later told them they were a thousand. Allah made each side look small to the other {trap}so the meeting would happen{/trap} and His decree would be carried out.
now: Your view of a situation is partial: the colleague you think is against you, the problem you think is tiny, the danger you think is huge. {idea}Your eyes give you a slice.{/idea} Hold your read of things a little more loosely, and return the matter to Allah.
old: I see this situation clearly. I know how it is.
new: My eyes show me a part. All matters return to Allah.
try: In one situation that worries you, list what you actually know versus what you assume.

title: In the hard moment: stand firm and remember Allah much.
subtitle: Two things to hold when pressure arrives

row.title: ask for wellbeing
sub: then be patient if it comes

then: The Prophet ﷺ once told the people: {idea}do not wish to meet the enemy, ask Allah for wellbeing,{/idea} but if you meet them, be patient. Ibn Kathir explains the verse as {reward}endurance, and never neglecting Allah's remembrance{/reward} in that moment, asking Him for help and trusting Him.
now: The diagnosis. The audit. The court date. You did not ask for this, and you should not have. Now it's here. {idea}Stay put, and keep Allah on your tongue.{/idea} Dhikr in the waiting room is the verse in your life.
old: When I'm under pressure, I don't have room for dhikr.
new: Under pressure is exactly when to remember Allah most.
try: Pick a short dhikr, like hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil, and repeat it during your next stressful moment.

title: Quarreling drains your strength. Be patient together.
subtitle: How a group loses its courage
then: Ibn Kathir explains the verse as {trap}avoiding dispute with one another, which leads to defeat and failure,{/trap} so their strength, endurance and courage would not leave them. The surah began with a quarrel over spoils, and here it names the cost of quarrels: {idea}be patient, Allah is with the patient.{/idea}
now: The family business where siblings fight over every decision. The mosque committee stuck for a year. The marriage where each argument restarts the last. {trap}The energy goes into the fight, not the work.{/trap} Patience with each other is strength.
old: Arguing it out is how we get things right.
new: Constant disputes drain us. Patience with each other keeps us strong.
try: In your next disagreement with someone close, let one point go that you would usually fight for.

title: Do not set out boastfully, to be seen by people.
subtitle: Marching for applause
then: When told the caravan was safe, Abu Jahl refused to turn back: {trap}we will go to Badr, slaughter camels, drink, and have singers, so the Arabs will always talk about us.{/trap} The believers are told {idea}not to be like those who went out boastful and showing off.{/idea}
now: The charity drive planned around the photo op. The Ramadan post. The big wedding meant to impress. {trap}Doing things so people will talk.{/trap} Check why you are going out the door.
old: If people see it, at least it inspires them.
new: Good deeds done for an audience lose what makes them good.
try: Do one good deed today that no one will ever find out about.

title: Shaytan promised to stand by them, then ran.
subtitle: The friend who disappears when it counts
then: Ibn Abbas said Shaytan came in the shape of Suraqah bin Malik and told Quraysh, {trap}no one will beat you today, I am your protector.{/trap} When he saw the angels, he pulled his hand away and fled, saying {idea}I see what you do not see, I fear Allah.{/idea}
now: The voice that says just this once, nobody will know, you deserve it. It cheers you all the way to the edge. {trap}Then the consequences come and it is nowhere.{/trap} Remember who left them standing alone at Badr.
old: This urge feels like it's on my side.
new: The voice that makes wrong look good always leaves when the bill arrives.
try: Next time a whisper makes something wrong look appealing, say a'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan and walk away.

title: Their religion has fooled them, the doubters said.
subtitle: When trusting Allah looks naive to others
then: Ash-Sha'bi said some in Makkah were considering Islam, but when they saw how few the Muslims were at Badr, they said {trap}their religion has deceived them.{/trap} The verse replies: {idea}whoever relies on Allah, Allah is Mighty and Wise.{/idea}
now: You turn down the deal that involves interest, the job with the shady side income, the shortcut everyone takes. Someone smirks: you're too religious, you'll never get ahead. {idea}Trust can look foolish from the outside.{/idea}
old: If people think my faith is naive, maybe they're right.
new: Relying on Allah may look naive to others. He is Mighty and Wise.
try: Next time your choice for Allah's sake is mocked, smile, stay calm, and quietly ask Allah to make it good.

title: If you could see the moment the angels take the soul.
subtitle: The hour of death for those who rejected

row.title: far away
sub: no need to think of it

then: The verse describes the moment death comes to those who rejected, with {trap}the angels striking and announcing the punishment.{/trap} Ibn Kathir notes that though it describes Badr, {idea}it is general for every disbeliever{/idea} at the time of death.
now: Every soul has that moment. It may come in a hospital bed or on an ordinary Tuesday. {idea}The point is not fear, it is preparation.{/idea} How you want to meet the angels is shaped by today's choices.
old: Death is something I'll think about when I'm older.
new: The moment of death is coming for me too. I want to meet it ready.
try: Ask yourself: if today were my last, what one thing would I fix? Fix it today.

title: This is what your own hands sent ahead.
subtitle: Allah is never unjust to His servants
then: The verse explains that the punishment is {trap}for what their hands put forward{/trap} in this life. Ibn Kathir quotes the hadith qudsi: {idea}My servants, it is your deeds I keep count of.{/idea} Whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise has only himself to blame.
now: You keep sending things ahead every day: the patience with your kids, the sharp words to your mother, the sadaqah, the cheating on the timesheet. {idea}It all arrives before you do.{/idea} The good news is that today you can send ahead something better.
old: What happens to me is out of my hands.
new: My deeds go ahead of me. Allah wrongs no one.
try: Send ahead one good deed today on purpose: a charity, a call to a parent, a kind word.

title: The same pattern as Pharaoh's people.
subtitle: Denying signs, and what follows
then: Ibn Kathir explains that those who fought the Prophet ﷺ were behaving like {trap}Pharaoh's people and earlier nations who rejected the messengers.{/trap} Allah dealt with them as He deals with their like. {idea}None can resist Him or escape His grasp.{/idea}
now: Patterns repeat in a life too. You ignore the first warning sign, then the second. The same argument, the same debt, the same regret, every few years. {idea}Notice the pattern before it becomes your story.{/idea}
old: History is about other people. My life is different.
new: Ignoring signs follows a pattern. I can notice mine and break it.
try: Identify one warning sign in your life you keep ignoring. Take it seriously today.

title: Allah does not take a blessing until people change themselves.
subtitle: Blessings stay with the grateful
then: Ibn Kathir calls this a statement of Allah's justice: {idea}He does not change a favor He has given except because of evil people commit.{/idea} He cites 13:11. Pharaoh's people lost {trap}their gardens, springs, treasures and fine homes{/trap} because of what they did. They wronged themselves.
now: The marriage that was warm and became cold. The job you once thanked Allah for and now only complain about. The health you stopped caring for. {idea}Before blaming the blessing, look at what changed in you.{/idea}
old: Good things just fade over time.
new: Blessings stay while I stay grateful. Change starts within me.
try: Pick one blessing you have taken for granted. Thank Allah for it and take care of it today.

title: They denied, so they were destroyed. All were wrongdoers.
subtitle: The pattern stated a second time
then: This repeats 8:52 with a change. There, they rejected the signs of Allah. Here, {trap}they denied the signs of their Lord,{/trap} the One who raised and provided for them. Ibn Kathir notes {idea}Allah did not wrong them, they wronged themselves.{/idea} Pharaoh's people were drowned.
now: Denying a gift from a stranger is one thing. Denying the One who has fed you since birth is another. {idea}Ingratitude toward your Lord is where it starts.{/idea} Notice how many of His gifts went unnoticed today.
old: I'm not denying anything. I just don't think about it much.
new: Forgetting my Lord's gifts is the first step toward denying them.
try: Before you sleep, name five things your Lord gave you today and say alhamdulillah for each.
